source.snippet: i use claude code daily and measured what pages cost it while doing research. an average wikipedia article is 68,240 tokens of raw html (tiktoken); nike's homepage is 353,000. claude code's built-in webfetch handles the easy case well. it summarizes wikipedia to about 950 tokens and clears cloudflare on some sites like indeed and ticketmaster. but on js-rendered and some anti-bot pages it returns nothing.

problem_statement: AI coding agents using web-fetch tools waste massive token budgets on raw HTML (68k–353k tokens per page) and return nothing on JS-rendered or anti-bot-protected pages, making agentic web research expensive and unreliable for developers paying per token.
target_segment: Software developers and solo operators using AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) on paid API plans who need reliable, token-efficient web content retrieval during agentic workflows.
notes: Poster is a daily paid Claude Code user who actively measured token consumption — clear paying buyer. Pain is quantified (68k raw vs 950 summarized). Gap: no reliable solution for JS-rendered pages returns nothing. A proxy/pre-processing service that delivers clean, token-minimal page content to AI agents would address this. Competitor surface: Firecrawl, Jina Reader — but agent-native integration with anti-bot bypass is the unmet piece. Signal strength capped at 3 because it's a single post; the underlying problem is widely discussed in the AI-dev community.
